svg.title: A client was pacing with clenched fists and shouting. The nurse used de-escalation techniques and offered a PRN medication. Which finding indicates that the intervention was effective?
svg.desc: Relaxed hands, a lowered voice, a seated posture, and accepting help are the objective markers that arousal has come down and the client has regained control. The client who stopped shouting but keeps pacing and striking his palm is the most tempting distractor because the noise decreased, but the motor agitation shows arousal is unchanged and assault may still be imminent. Silent staring is an ominous sign that can precede an attack, and withdrawing while refusing all contact is not resolution.
